blocks.passage:
Ethics at work are tested in small, ordinary moments far more often than in dramatic ones. A gift that feels slightly too generous. A question from a client about another client. A request to sign off on something you have not actually reviewed. These are the moments where integrity is quietly built or quietly lost.

Good companies make the right choice easier, by providing clear policies and safe channels to raise concerns. Good professionals make the right choice automatic, by deciding in advance what they will and will not do. "I don't accept gifts over £50" is much easier to say than "well, I'll think about it", because there is no thinking to do — the decision was already made.

Compliance is the legal minimum. Ethics is the private standard you hold yourself to when the legal minimum is clearly not enough. In the long run, clients can smell the difference.

items.why: "Ethics at work are tested in small, ordinary moments far more often than in dramatic ones."

items.why: "by providing clear policies and safe channels to raise concerns."

audio.text:
For today's compliance refresher, I'm not going to use dramatic fraud examples. The real tests are much smaller and much more common, so let's talk about those.

First one. A supplier sends you a very generous gift at Christmas — well over our fifty-pound limit. It feels rude to send it back. But our gift policy exists precisely so you don't have to decide in the moment. You disclose it, you decline it politely, and the policy takes the awkwardness off you.

Second. A client asks you, casually, how another client is pricing. That's a conflict of interest, and the answer is always the same: we don't discuss one client's business with another. Full stop.

Third, and this is the one that catches good people. Someone asks you to sign off on a report you haven't actually read, because they're in a hurry. Your signature means you checked it. If you haven't, you must not sign — no matter who's asking.

If anything ever feels off, we have a confidential channel. Raising a concern early is always cheaper than a reputational problem later.

items.q: Why does Charlotte avoid dramatic fraud examples?
options: The real tests are smaller and much more common
They are too rare to matter
items.why: "The real tests are much smaller and much more common."

items.q: What should you do with a gift over the fifty-pound limit?
options: Disclose it and decline it politely
items.why: "You disclose it, you decline it politely, and the policy takes the awkwardness off you."

items.q: What is the answer when a client asks how another client is pricing?
options: We don't discuss one client's business with another
items.why: "we don't discuss one client's business with another. Full stop."

items.q: What does Charlotte say about signing off on an unread report?
options: You must not sign — your signature means you checked it
items.why: "Your signature means you checked it. If you haven't, you must not sign."

items.q: What does Charlotte say about raising a concern early?
options: It is always cheaper than a reputational problem later
items.why: "Raising a concern early is always cheaper than a reputational problem later."

items.q: "She acted with **integrity**." Integrity means…
items.why: Integrity = integridade.

items.q: A **conflict of interest** is a situation where…
options: your private interest could improperly influence your professional duty
items.why: Conflict of interest = conflito de interesses.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "You must **___** any gift over the limit."
items.why: To disclose = divulgar, declarar.

items.q: The **code of conduct** is…
options: the set of rules on how to behave professionally
items.why: Code of conduct = código de conduta.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Mishandling this could create serious **___** for the firm."
items.why: Reputational risk = risco reputacional.

items.q: "If something feels off, **speak up**." To speak up means to…
items.why: Speak up = manifestar-se, levantar a questão.

items.q: "We must **draw the line** at accepting large gifts." To draw the line means to…
options: set a limit on what is acceptable
items.why: Draw the line = estabelecer o limite.

items.q: "Don't just **turn a blind eye** to it." To turn a blind eye means to…
items.why: Turn a blind eye = fazer vista grossa.

items.q: "I won't **sign off on** something I haven't read." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente.

items.q: "Let's **play it by the book** on this one." To play it by the book means to…
items.why: Play it by the book = seguir as regras à risca.
